component.name: Amplia
component.summary: Audio player for Linux in the spirit of Winamp
Tocador de áudio para Linux com a alma do Winamp

description.p: Amplia is a native audio player for Linux with the behaviour people remember from Winamp: one window, a playlist that plays, an equalizer, and no browser in the middle.
It is a new player, not a port and not a copy — the code is written from scratch and the inspired-by surface is the one that made that player comfortable to use.

ul.li: Plays MP3, AAC/M4A, FLAC, Ogg Vorbis, Opus and WAV, gapless, with bitrate, sample rate and channels on the display.
Playlist with ordering, shuffle, repeat, drag to reorder, fonts and per-track metadata.
A single queue for what comes next, with the origin of each entry: playlist, library or radio.
Local library with SQLite: search, filters by artist, album and genre, ratings, play counts and views for recently added, played and most played.
Mood radio: a target between agitation and key, with stability and a blend of mood and listening history, plus local radio from the track playing.
10-band equalizer, themes, ReplayGain, MPRIS, tray icon, Last.fm and ListenBrainz scrobbling.
Help, tag editor and about window, in Portuguese and English.

ul.li: The library has a schema version, and opening a newer database warns instead of showing an empty library.
The volume slider ends where the total time counter ends; the tree title is no longer a view.
English is complete: 522 translated texts, none pending.

description.p: Complete English, including the library window and the mood names.
